survey: Gold five-pointed sheriff star badge, rotated in the picture plane and seen almost face-on, floating against a purple sunburst with no ground. Each point is beveled into two facets that meet along a center ridge running from the hub out to the tip. Each tip ends in a gold ball attached at the point. These read as spheres, lit and shaded alike, so viewpoint does not affect them. A red domed gem sits in a round bezel at the center. Because the badge faces the camera, the bezel is a near-circle, which fits. A thin raised rim runs around the outline at an even width, which also fits a face-on view. The points are a little uneven in length and spacing. That reads as a stylized hand-drawn shape, not a tilted surface, since the rim and gem show no foreshortening that would conflict with it. With no ground plane, contact cannot conflict with anything.
